phase_name: Fixture tests for Classes F and G

objectives.description: Class F fixture: missing/null/empty candidates all fire, null also fires Class B
Class G fixture: glob candidate fires, control candidate does not
Negative fixture: all clean -> both sections print explicit negatives
--repair fixture: candidate missing file_scope key -> no write, key stays absent

approaches_tried.approach: wrote the --repair D4 fixture expecting it to trivially pass against the already-implemented D4 guarantee
approaches_tried.reason: the fixture instead revealed a genuine pre-existing bug: --repair's write filter used plain .field == null (no has() guard), so an absent key on a candidate sharing an invocation with a genuinely-null sibling was silently manufactured to []. Confirmed via manual reproduction, then confirmed pre-existing via git show against the pre-Task-163 commit. Fixed the write filter and its preview print to gate on has(field) and .field == null for both dependencies and file_scope.

deviations.description: --repair fixture: a candidate with no file_scope key -> no write, key still absent afterwards (the D4 guarantee, asserted rather than assumed)
deviations.reason: MAJOR: this fixture caught a genuine, pre-existing (not introduced by this task) bug in --repair's write filter -- an absent key on a candidate co-invoked with a genuinely-null sibling was silently manufactured to []. Fixed the underlying bug (gating the write transform and preview on has(field) AND .field == null, not plain .field == null) rather than merely writing a fixture that would have failed against production code. This is a correctness fix to the EXISTING Class B repair machinery, not a new repair branch for Classes F/G, which remain untouched by --repair per D4/Non-Goals.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: MAJOR, altered — a genuine pre-existing bug was discovered and fixed, not merely a new fixture added)*
